newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Detroit mayor Young battles pneumonia.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Detroit mayor Young battles pneumonia.

text.p: Former Detroit mayor Coleman Young, battling a recurrence of pneumonia, was listed in serious condition at Sinai Hospital on Wednesday but his condition had begun to improve, a spokesman said.

Young, 79, who has long suffered from emphysema, was admitted to the hospital last week for rehabilitation therapy, but "took a turn for the worse" on Monday night, said Bob Berg, his former press secretary.

"He's still listed as serious but the doctors say there's been a significant improvement," Berg said. "I had a chance to see him this morning and he's awake, alert and the twinkle is back in his eye."
Young, the city's first black mayor, retired at the end of 1993 after 20 years in office. A longtime smoker, he has frequently suffered respiratory ailments.
In March 1995, he was in the hospital for 10 days with a minor stroke.
